From: Lily Chen <lily.chen@healthsync.ai>

Subject: Intermittent chat stalls + 429 spikes during peak hours

Marcus —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 429s and full chat stalls on our production integration between 08:45–09:15 PT this morning. Some sessions show repeated client retries (3–6x) before either succeeding or the client giving up; others remain stuck with an idle stream and the UI shows "Waiting for response..." for >30s. Overall user-reported latency doubled and automated throughput dropped by ~20% during the window.

Attached are request logs and a sample heap snapshot. We haven't made any change on our side. Can you confirm whether this matches any cluster issues on your side? This is affecting a handful of high-value customers; we need a rapid remediation plan and executive visibility if this is platform-level.

Thanks,
Lily Chen
Head of Integrations — HealthSync

From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent chat stalls + 429 spikes during peak hours

Marcus / Lauren — quick triage notes from infra:

- Observed a 12:43–12:50 UTC window (08:43–08:50 PT) with a sudden 5xx/429 surge across two frontend load balancer pods servicing default routing.
- Autoscaler reacted but scaling lagged by ~18s because the dominant request pattern was many short-lived streaming connects rather than long-lived CPU-heavy requests; warmstart limits prevented immediate extra runtime slots.
- A misconfigured backoff on an older client library caused some clients to retry aggressively (tight exponential with low jitter), which amplified the load and triggered short-term queue pressure.
- We also saw a small number of idle TCP resets from a kernel-level keepalive bump in one host that caused streaming sessions to silently drop; those clients retried from the UI and hit the rate limiter.

Action items we executed:
1) Temporarily increased concurrent streaming slots for the affected pool and disabled the aggressive rate-limiter rule for HS-workspace (mitigates immediate 429s).
2) Flushed prefix cache for a subset of routing entries to reduce queuing pressure.
3) Opened RED-9123 (link below) to track root cause and a permanent fix (workload-aware scaling + improved client backoff guidance).

I'll keep this thread open; recommend we prepare an exec note for HS and copy Sales leadership.

— Aditya
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: Lily Chen <lily.chen@healthsync.ai>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@healthsync.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Incident update + next steps (RED-9123) — HealthSync impact

Lily / Rajiv — thanks again for flagging this. Summary and next steps below.

Timeline
- 08:43 PT (12:43 UTC) — sudden burst of short-lived streaming connects from multiple HealthSync hosts; connection pattern shows tight client-side retries.
- 08:43–09:10 PT — load balancer queue pressure increased; 429s surfaced when rate limiter hit threshold.
- 08:50 PT — infra increased concurrent streaming slots and relaxed per-workspace rate limit (temporary mitigation).

Impact
- User-facing: intermittent stalls where UI reported "Waiting for response" > 15s for affected sessions; estimated 350 sessions retried and ~20% spike in retry attempts during 27-minute window.
- Business: estimated 6–8% throughput reduction for HealthSync during the incident window; we recognize this impacted paid users.

Immediate remediation taken (live)
- Temporary increase to streaming concurrency for your workspace and suppression of the aggressive rate-limiter rule.
- Cleared queuing backlog and applied conservative backoff at edge for retried requests.
- Eng traced idle TCP resets to a host kernel keepalive bump; hotfix applied to normalize keepalive on the affected hosts.

Permanent fixes planned (tracking: RED-9123)
- Workload-aware warmstart improvements to reduce scaling lag for streaming-heavy workloads (ETA: 3 weeks for initial rollout).
- Runtime-level detection for retry storms with automatic per-session dampening (ETA: 4 weeks).
- Updated client-backoff guidance and a small SDK patch to add jitter by default (we will provide a compatibility-safe patch in 2 weeks).

Customer asks and proposed credits
- Lauren / Sergio are coordinating the goodwill credit recommendation. We propose a small usage credit for the incident window and a priority rollout lane for the warmstart patch.

Next steps for HealthSync
1) We will provide a post-incident report (detailed logs, timelines, and root cause analysis) within 48 hours.
2) Provide the SDK backoff patch and recommended config changes within 2 weeks.
3) Schedule a technical review with HealthSync engineers to verify mitigations and pilot warmstart improvements.

Please let us know if you'd prefer a synchronous review this week — we can make time. Apologies for the disruption and thank you for your patience.

— Marcus Lin
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
